subtitle: Santivarma and the Birth of the Triparvatha Line

panels.shot: sweeping low-angle wide of a king framed by three distant hill-forts
panels.action: Santivarma stands in regal stillness, a single crown on his head but three looming hill-forts shimmer behind him on the horizon, as if they too were crowns weighing upon his shoulders in a dusky Deccan landscape.

dialogue.text: In the stone of Talagunda he is praised as wearing three crowns, yet Santivarma’s greatest act split his own house and birthed the shadowy realm of Triparvatha.

i18n.hi: तालगुंड के पत्थर पर उसे तीन मुकुट वाला कहा, पर शांतिवर्मा का सबसे बड़ा काम था अपना ही घर बाँटकर त्रिपर्वत जैसा छाया–राज बनाना।

panels.shot: slow push-in on inscription being carved with king watching
panels.action: In a sunlit courtyard at Talagunda, artisans chisel a tall stone pillar while Santivarma watches, arms folded, his face calm but intent, the forested edge of the Western Ghats rising beyond.

dialogue.text: Around 450 CE, in the Brahmana village of Talagunda, a Kadamba king ordered his story cut into stone, calling on the poet Kubja to bind his name to eternity.

i18n.hi: लगभग 450 ईस्वी में, ब्राह्मण ग्राम तालगुंड में, एक कदंब राजा ने कवि कुब्ज को पुकारा, ताकि उसका किस्सा पत्थर पर खुदकर अमर हो जाए।

panels.shot: medium shot over Santivarma’s shoulder toward the sculptor and half-finished pillar
panels.action: Seen from behind Santivarma’s broad shoulders, the chisel bites into the pillar, faint lines of script emerging as a sculptor kneels, sweat on his brow, the half-finished shaft rising like a pale tree against the sky.

dialogue.text: This Talagunda pillar, later read by scholars like Kielhorn, would remember Santivarma as the son of Kakusthavarma, a king adorned, it says, with three shining crowns.

i18n.hi: यह तालगुंड स्तंभ, जिसे बाद में कीलहॉर्न जैसे विद्वानों ने पढ़ा, शांतिवर्मा को ककुत्सवर्मा का पुत्र मानता है, उस राजा का, जो तीन दमकते मुकुटों से सजा बताया गया।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on Santivarma’s face, eyes reflecting three vague crowns
panels.action: A close view of Santivarma’s thoughtful face shows in his dark eyes the faint mirrored shapes of three coronets, as if imagined, his jaw set between pride and burden.

dialogue.text: Were these crowns just words for glory, or the memory of real diadems, of real thrones in Banavasi and beyond that Kakusthavarma had once bent to Kadamba power?

i18n.hi: ये मुकुट सिर्फ शौर्य की बातें थे, या सचमुच राजमुकुट, वे सिंहासन जिनको बनवासी से परे तक ककुत्सवर्मा ने कदंब सत्ता के आगे झुकाया था?

panels.shot: bird’s-eye wide of Banavasi city and palace complex amid forests and river
panels.action: From high above, the old capital Banavasi spreads along the Varada river, with tiled roofs, temple spires and a timbered palace compound, encircled by moats and earthen ramparts amid thick green forest.

dialogue.text: Banavasi was the heart of Kadamba power, a forest kingdom turned royal city, grown strong under Mayurasharma and Kakusthavarma between the pull of Pallava and the shadow of the Vakatakas.

i18n.hi: बनवासी कदंब शक्ति का दिल था, जंगल से उठा राजनगर, जिसे मयूरशर्मा और ककुत्सवर्मा ने पल्लव के खिंचाव और वाकाटक छाया के बीच मजबूत किया।

panels.shot: medium interior shot of throne room with counselors and maps laid on a low table
panels.action: In a carved wooden hall, Santivarma sits on a low lion-legged throne while counselors stand by rolled palm-leaf charters and a painted map of the western Deccan, its edges marked with tiny hill symbols and fort signs.

dialogue.text: Santivarma inherited a realm woven by alliances, Kadamba charters at Halasi and beyond showing lineages and grants, even as Pallava power pressed from the east and frontier hills stirred in the west.

i18n.hi: शांतिवर्मा को वही राज्य मिला जो रिश्तों से बुना था; हलसी और आगे के कदंब ताम्रपत्रों में वंश और दान दिखते हैं, जबकि पूरब से पल्लव दबाव और पश्चिम की पहाड़ियाँ उथल–पुथल में थीं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on map segment showing Banavasi and a rough ‘Triparvatha’ hill cluster
panels.action: The camera closes on a section of the painted map where Banavasi sits marked by a stylised temple and, farther north-east, a cluster of three hill symbols is circled in red pigment by a court hand.

dialogue.text: Later scholars like Moraes and Karashima would search these hills for Triparvatha, debating whether it lay near present-day Dharwad, another node in the chain of Deccan strongholds.

i18n.hi: मोरायस और काराशिमा जैसे विद्वान बाद में इन्हीं पहाड़ियों में त्रिपर्वत खोजते रहे, बहस करते कि वह आज के धारवाड़ के पास था या किसी और दक्कनी गढ़ की कड़ी।

panels.shot: medium shot of Santivarma in discussion with a younger warrior-prince-like figure (shown only in silhouette, unnamed)
panels.action: Inside the dim hall, Santivarma leans forward, one hand resting on the map, as a younger, armored prince’s silhouette stands before him, the light from a lattice throwing bars across them both.

dialogue.text: The inscriptions do not narrate his councils, yet the later rise of a Krishnavarma at Triparvatha hints at a younger cadet branch coming into its own under the weight of growing threats.

i18n.hi: शिलालेख उसकी सभाओं का हाल नहीं कहते, पर त्रिपर्वत के कृष्णवर्मा का बाद का उदय बताता है कि कोई छोटा शाखा–राजकुमार बढ़ते खतरे में अपनी राह बना रहा था।

panels.shot: low-angle medium shot of Santivarma placing a small crown beside his own on a ritual tray
panels.action: By a flickering oil lamp, Santivarma gently sets a second, smaller crown next to his own on a silver tray before a deity, his broad hand lingering over the metal as priests chant softly in the shadows.

dialogue.text: Some modern historians see in his three crowns a sign that one Kadamba realm was being shared, the main line at Banavasi and a cadet at Triparvatha, dividing authority between centre and frontier.

i18n.hi: कुछ आधुनिक इतिहासकार इन तीन मुकुटों में संकेत देखते हैं कि एक ही कदंब राज्य बँटकर चल रहा था — मुख्य राज बनवासी में, शाखा त्रिपर्वत में — जहां सत्ता बीच और सीमा में बँटी थी।

panels.shot: wide shot of a rugged hill-fort landscape with a garrison drilling, Santivarma in the foreground
panels.action: On a rocky hill with stone walls and wooden palisades, soldiers drill with spears as Santivarma stands at the edge of the rampart, cloak snapping in the wind, watching the frontier fort come alive under grey skies.

dialogue.text: To guard these hills from Pallava raids and rival chiefs, a second seat of power at Triparvatha may have seemed wise, a shield turned outward even as it created another centre of loyalty.

i18n.hi: पल्लव धावों और सीमावर्ती सरदारों से इन पहाड़ियों की रखवाली को, त्रिपर्वत में दूसरा शक्ति–आसन रखना समझदारी लगा होगा, बाहर की ओर ढाल, पर भीतर एक नया निष्ठा–केन्द्र।

panels.shot: close-up on Santivarma’s hand resting on the rough stone of a hill bastion, distant plains visible
panels.action: Santivarma’s hand presses firmly against the weathered stone of a bastion, veins visible, as beyond the battlements the hazy plains stretch towards an unseen east where enemy banners might rise.

dialogue.speaker: santivarma
dialogue.text: A house that holds the hills holds its fate. But will it hold together?

i18n.hi: जो घर पहाड़ थामे, वही अपनी किस्मत थामता है। सवाल ये है, घर खुद कितना थमेगा?

panels.shot: medium interior shot of priests and scribes preparing copper plates, Santivarma overseeing
panels.action: In a quiet chamber, scribes engrave palm-size copper plates with fine script while priests bless them with sandalwood paste; Santivarma stands behind, half in shadow, eyes moving over the gleaming metal.

dialogue.text: Copper plates from Halasi, later studied by G.S. Gai, trace how power flowed after Santivarma, naming successors in Banavasi even as another line at Triparvatha began to leave its own imprints.

i18n.hi: हलसी के ताम्रपट, जिन्हें बाद में जी.एस. गाय ने पढ़ा, दिखाते हैं कि शांतिवर्मा के बाद शक्ति कैसे बही, बनवासी के उत्तराधिकारियों के साथ–साथ त्रिपर्वत की अलग छापें भी उभरती हैं।

panels.shot: wide shot of a ceremonial assembly with two thrones set slightly apart
panels.action: In a grand hall open to the courtyard, two thrones stand upon a dais, one slightly higher; Santivarma occupies the main seat while the second remains empty, draped with a ceremonial cloth, watched by curious nobles.

dialogue.text: The record is silent on a formal division, yet the later coexistence of Banavasi and Triparvatha branches suggests that under Santivarma the seeds of a shared sovereignty were sown.

i18n.hi: दस्तावेज़ साफ–साफ बँटवारे की बात नहीं करते, पर बनवासी और त्रिपर्वत शाखाओं का साथ–साथ चलना बताता है कि शांतिवर्मा के समय ही साझा सत्ता के बीज बोए गए थे।

panels.shot: medium shot with soft focus, Santivarma slightly older, looking at the Talagunda pillar now fully raised
panels.action: Years later, an older Santivarma stands before the completed Talagunda pillar, its surface dense with script, the forest wind tugging at his cloak as he lifts his head to read the lines that praise him.

dialogue.text: Verse by verse, the Talagunda inscription weaves his lineage, tracing Mayurasharma’s rise and Kakusthavarma’s alliances, then resting on Santivarma, the king who shines, it claims, with the splendour of three crowns.

i18n.hi: तालगुंड शिलालेख श्लोक दर श्लोक उसका वंश बुनता है, मयूरशर्मा का उदय, ककुत्सवर्मा की संधियाँ, और अंत में शांतिवर्मा पर टिकता है — उस राजा पर जो, वह कहता है, तीन मुकुटों की चमक में दमकता था।

panels.shot: extreme close-up on a specific line of the inscription, letters crisp and deep
panels.action: The chisel-cut letters of the pillar fill the frame, their shadows sharp in the sun, a single line standing out where the term likening Santivarma to bearing three crowns is carved deeper and more boldly.

dialogue.text: Later readers in distant libraries would pause at this phrase, puzzling over what these ‘three crowns’ meant in practice, and how they foreshadowed the branching of the Kadamba house.

i18n.hi: दूर–दराज़ की लाइब्रेरियों में बाद के पाठक इसी पंक्ति पर अटक गए, सोचते रहे कि ये ‘तीन मुकुट’ असल में क्या थे, और कैसे उन्होंने कदंब घराने की शाखाओं का संकेत दिया।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot half-shadowed: one side Banavasi palace, other side a hill-fort labeled by architecture as different seat
panels.action: In a split composition, the left half shows Banavasi’s palace under clear light while the right half shows a distinct hill-fort city under darker clouds, Santivarma’s faint silhouette straddling the divide like a fading watermark.

dialogue.text: After his time, the Banavasi line and the Triparvatha line stood side by side, sometimes cooperating, sometimes colliding, their grants and titles revealing a realm both defended and divided.

i18n.hi: उसके बाद बनवासी और त्रिपर्वत दोनों वंश कंधे से कंधा रहे — कभी साथ, कभी टकराहट में — उनके दानपत्र और उपाधियाँ दिखाती हैं कि राज्य एक साथ बचा भी और बँटा भी।

panels.shot: medium shot in a darkened council hall, two groups of nobles facing each other warily, empty throne between
panels.action: In a shadowed hall, nobles bearing different emblems stand in two clusters facing each other across an empty throne, their faces wary, while above them a beam of light falls on a carved Kadamba crest.

dialogue.text: The Halasi plates of Mrigeshavarma hint at later conflicts, the calm legal formulas of donations masking struggles over precedence and control between branches that shared a name but not always a will.

i18n.hi: मृगेशवर्मा के हलसी ताम्रपट बाद की टकराहटों की आहट देते हैं; दान के सधे कानूनी शब्दों के पीछे, उसी नाम के दो वंशों के बीच अग्रता और पकड़ की खींचतान छुपी है।

panels.shot: slow pull-back from Santivarma’s statue-like image fading into bare pillar and scattered ruins
panels.action: Santivarma appears like a statue for a moment, seated in regal pose, then as the view pulls back he fades into the weathered Talagunda pillar standing alone amid broken stones and grass under a vast sky.

dialogue.text: Santivarma’s own end slips through the gaps of time; what endures is stone and copper, from which historians must reconstruct how a king holding three crowns left behind a house with more than one throne.

i18n.hi: शांतिवर्मा का अपना अंत समय की दरारों से फिसल गया; जो बचा है वह पत्थर और ताँबा है, जिनसे इतिहासकार गढ़ते हैं कि तीन मुकुट सँभालने वाला राजा कैसे कई सिंहासनों वाला घर छोड़ गया।

panels.shot: high wide shot of modern scholars at a table with photos of inscriptions, Santivarma’s ghostly outline above
panels.action: In a modern study lit by lamps, scholars bend over photographs of the Talagunda pillar and Halasi plates, their desks crowded with books by Moraes and Karashima, while above them, faint and translucent, Santivarma’s outline watches in silence.

dialogue.text: His story reminds us that sharing power can be a fortress and a fault-line, and that even in our time, every divided realm carries the echo of Santivarma’s three unseen crowns.

i18n.hi: उसकी कहानी याद दिलाती है कि बाँटी हुई सत्ता एक साथ किला भी है और दरार भी, और आज के हर बँटे हुए राज्य में शांतिवर्मा के उन तीन अदृश्य मुकुटों की गूँज अब भी सुनाई देती है।

title_i18n.en: Three Crowns and a Divided Realm

subtitle_i18n.en: Santivarma and the Birth of the Triparvatha Line
